The test image shows a close-up of a plant surface (appears to be a fruit or stem) covered in dense, fluffy, grayish-white mycelium with small dark specks visible beneath. This fuzzy, cottony growth is highly characteristic of **Gray Mold** (Botrytis cinerea).

Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image (Bugwood_22) shows a different symptom expression (ghost spotting on fruit surface), but that's a different stage of gray mold. The test image shows the classic dense, fluffy, grayish-tan mycelium — the signature of Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold). The webby hyphal network and dark speck-like structures beneath are highly characteristic. Sclerotinia would be brighter white and more cotton-like; Rhizopus would have coarser mycelium with distinct black sporangia.
